newsitem.title: FRANCE: French AIDS group rejects far-right mayor's funds.
newsitem.headline: French AIDS group rejects far-right mayor's funds.

text.p: A hotline for AIDS patients in the southern town of Vitrolles said on Thursday it had rejected a subsidy from the municipality which is controlled by the extreme-right National Front.

Sida Info Service said in a statement it would rather do without the money -- a mere 1,000 francs ($160) -- than accept it from anti-immigrant mayor Catherine Megret whose principles are "fundamentally different" from those of the group.

"When there is social exclusion, health problems, especially those linked to HIV-infection, become even more serious, relegating the vulnerable people concerned to the state of touchables," it said in a statement.
Sida Info Service said the municipality had deposited the money directly into the group's bank account even though it had not asked for a subsidy.

The French government announced this week it was giving 50,000 francs ($81,000) to non-profit associations in Vitrolles to help make up for some five million francs ($810,000) of subsidies that Megret has withdrawn.

Vitrolles is one of four towns controlled by the Front, which advocates sending home some three million immigrants, most of them North Africans, and reserving jobs and welfare for French-born citizens.

National Front mayors have halted municipal subsidies to several cultural or anti-racist organisations in the towns they control. Some have had school cafeterias stop making special meals for Moslem and Jewish children. ($ = 6.18 French Francs)
